# MM-P2-L3-HT02 Maintenance manual - Machining heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
- This manual covers routine maintenance, verification, and documentation practices for Machining heat treat furnace #2, EQ-P2-L3-HT02. It applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for furnace reliability, thermal uniformity, and safety in the P2, line P2-L3 work area.
- Exclusions: major rebuilds, control system replacement beyond modular component swap, and vendor factory repairs. For those activities, contact engineering and reference service bulletins SB-1023 and SB-1045.

Background and rationale
- The furnace supports machining hardening cycles where metallurgical outcomes depend on accurate austenitizing temperature and stable soak profiles. Drift in control elements or sensing circuits leads to out-of-spec microstructure and rework.
- Maintaining sensor accuracy and control integrity reduces scrap, improves process repeatability, and preserves tool life downstream. The thermocouple sensing network and control setpoint are primary process inputs and therefore subject to scheduled verification and adjustment.

Key settings and intervals
- The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C.
- The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.

Tools and supplies
- Portable reference thermocouple and calibrated data logger with certificate traceable to laboratory standards. Use the reference channel for comparison only.
- Insulating gloves, face shield, and heat-resistant tools as per plant PPE requirements.
- Non conductive handheld multimeter for sensor circuit continuity checks.
- Small hand tools for terminal access and clamp adjustment.
- Calibration stickers and log forms for records.
- Replacement thermocouple assemblies and mounting hardware as stocked for EQ-P2-L3-HT02.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Confirm authorization to enter the heat treat area and lockout as required by plant safety procedures. Coordinate with production to isolate furnace cycles.
  - Review related documents SOP-P2-L3-03 for operational controls and SB-1023 and SB-1045 for any known service notes that affect inspection or parts.
  - Verify availability of the portable reference thermocouple and its calibration certificate before work begins.

- Visual and mechanical inspection
  - With furnace de-energized per plant lockout requirements, inspect thermocouple sheath routing, anchor points, and electrical terminations for signs of wear, corrosion, or loose connections.
  - Check furnace door seals and refractory conditions at accessible locations to confirm no local hot spots that could affect sensor readings.

- Thermocouple verification and calibration
  - Install the portable reference thermocouple in the process zone adjacent to the installed process thermocouple location, using the same mounting arrangement where practicable to minimize spatial gradients.
  - Bring the furnace up to the austenitizing setpoint defined above, following SOP-P2-L3-03 for controlled ramp and soak. Monitor both reference logger and process controller readings concurrently.
  - Compare the process thermocouple output to the portable reference over the soak period. If the deviation exceeds acceptable drift noted in SOP-P2-L3-03, replace the process thermocouple assembly and retest.
  - Record the comparison trace on the calibration log and attach the portable reference certificate to the maintenance record.

- Control verification
  - Confirm the controller is commanding the setpoint value specified above and that output influences heater elements as described in SOP-P2-L3-03.
  - Validate alarm thresholds and operator interface setpoints to ensure they match process documentation.

- Post-calibration actions
  - Apply calibration sticker indicating next calibration due per the interval specified above and record the action in the equipment maintenance log.
  - Return the furnace to normal operation in coordination with production and note any deviations or corrective actions in the shift handover log.

Examples and troubleshooting notes
- Example: If the process thermocouple reads lower than the portable reference by a consistent offset, suspect connector corrosion or sheath degradation. Tighten or replace termination hardware, then repeat verification. If offset persists after terminal work, replace the thermocouple assembly.
- Example: If controller display reads the setpoint correctly but the actual chamber temperature lags during soak, inspect element load distribution and refractory for insulation loss. Document findings and escalate to engineering if replacement is required; reference SB-1023 for element failure guidance.
- If intermittent sensor readings occur only during door operation, check for mechanical stress at the mounting point and secure the probe to prevent flexing.

Records to keep
- Attach to the EQ-P2-L3-HT02 maintenance file:
  - Calibration log and portable reference certificate for each verification event.
  - Inspection checklist documenting visual observations and any replaced parts.
  - Controller output and reference logger trace for the soak at the austenitizing setpoint.
  - Copy of completed calibration sticker photograph showing next calibration due per the thermocouple interval above.
  - Any deviation reports and corrective action records, including cross-reference to SB-1023, SB-1045, and SOP-P2-L3-03 where applicable.

Acceptance criteria
- After maintenance and verification, the furnace meets the following:
  - Controller displays the austenitizing setpoint specified above and maintains stable control during soak as evidenced by reference logger trace.
  - Process thermocouple agrees with the portable reference within the acceptance window defined in SOP-P2-L3-03 for the full soak duration.
  - Thermocouple has been calibrated and documented according to the interval specified above with sticker and maintenance log entry present.
  - No active mechanical defects or loose electrical terminations remain at the probe mounting and connection points.

Related documents
- SB-1023
- SB-1045
- SOP-P2-L3-03

End of document.
